scope: R,F,H substantive positive results and R/G/F limitations; root handles G2–7 and M/T foundations.

sources.title: Nonsmooth Variants of Powell’s BFGS Convergence Theorem
sources.access: Author-hosted complete journal manuscript, theorem statements and proofs read; publisher publication history checked.
sources.paraphrase: Corollary 4.2 establishes full-BFGS convergence on the Euclidean norm in arbitrary dimension. Corollary 4.4 obtains only a subsequence reaching the nonsmooth axis for u²+|v|; full convergence is left open. The proof constructs a convex smooth extension agreeing on an objective band, preserving the BFGS sequence, and applies Powell’s theorem.
sources.version_note: March19 Optimization Online posting predates March20 arXiv submission; original preprint title BFGS convergence to nonsmooth minimizers of convex functions.

sources.title: Nonsmooth optimization via quasi-Newton methods
sources.first_public_date: 2008-12 (related predecessor; exact date/version identity not established)
sources.access: Author-hosted published article, relevant full text read.
sources.paraphrase: The planar Euclidean-norm analysis uses exact line search. Scalar absolute-value analysis uses a specified bracketing/bisection secant algorithm and initially c1=0, measuring function trials. Theorem 4.5 concerns scalar ray differentiability, with a bounded-below absolutely continuous ray; Proposition 4.11 gives an interval of acceptable steps after deleting scalar nondifferentiability points. These do not imply full-space differentiability along every ray.
sources.version_note: Journal volume is 2013; online publication is February16 2012. Older bfgs_inexactLS.pdf has different title and numbering and was not conflated with the final article.

sources.title: Technical Results on the Convergence of Quasi-Newton Methods for Nonsmooth Optimization
sources.access: Open-access publisher full text and arXiv v1 read.
sources.paraphrase: The published theorem assumes an iterate limit, bounds the eigenvalues outside the jump span, and assumes annihilation of gradient jumps. Its local criticality theorem also uses stable active-gradient geometry. The proof passes to matrix accumulation points and uses kernel membership and Wolfe decrease. The article still identifies unconditional BFGS convergence of u²+|v| as unresolved; the eigenvalue assumptions are not proved.
sources.version_note: Edition cites the 2025 preprint; update bibliography to JOTA209, article57(2026). Journal theorem numbering differs.

sources.title: On the convergence of BFGS on a class of piecewise linear non-smooth functions
sources.access: Primary arXiv full text, statements and proof read.
locators: §IV main Theorem IV.1 and following remarks
sources.paraphrase: Invertible affine invariance is explicit. For the unbounded two-piece common-tilt model, scalar recurrences from reflected BFGS matrices and Armijo decrease force finite termination at a direction exposing unboundedness. An infinite-run many-piece value assertion is a different, weaker conclusion on the two-piece specialization.
sources.version_note: No journal publication date established here; do not invent one.

sources.title: A simple proof of the Baillon–Haddad theorem on open subsets of Hilbert spaces
sources.access: Primary arXiv full text, Theorem2.5 and proof read.
sources.paraphrase: On an open convex Hilbert domain, convex differentiable L-smoothness and 1/L-cocoercivity are equivalent. This is exactly the established smooth-gradient inequality used as a component of the centered-family proof, not a new BFGS convergence theorem.

sources.title: Partial smoothness and constant rank
sources.access: Primary arXiv full text, normal-space section inspected.
locators: §5 normal bundle and partial smoothness; Theorem5.1
sources.paraphrase: Provides established tangent/normal and identifiable-manifold background. It does not state convergence of every unmodified BFGS run on the report’s finite polyhedral partitions.
sources.version_note: The cited/read 2018 arXiv v1 has two authors. The published successor is A. S. Lewis, Jingwei Liang, Tonghua Tian, SIAM J Optim32(1)276–291(2022), DOI10.1137/19M1237909. Do not transfer preprint theorem numbering unverified to the journal edition.

sources.title: Clustering with Bregman Divergences
sources.paraphrase: Definition1 gives the standard Bregman supporting-plane expression for a strictly convex generator differentiable on its relative interior, and credits Bregman1967. The report uses the same algebraic expression at a differentiable second endpoint without strict convexity; this is ordinary convex supporting-plane calculus, not a claimed new divergence.

sources.title: A Singular Value Thresholding Algorithm for Matrix Completion
sources.access: Primary arXiv Theorem2.1 and proof read; publisher dates checked.
sources.paraphrase: The proximal minimizer of half the squared Frobenius distance plus a nuclear-norm penalty is obtained by singular-value soft thresholding. The proof uses the nuclear-norm subgradient formula. Consequently R’s optimizer diag(1,0) for data diag(2,0) and unit penalty is an immediate known special case; the radial-criterion obstruction is separate.

sources.title: A Quasi-Newton Approach to Nonsmooth Convex Optimization Problems in Machine Learning
sources.access: Primary JMLR abstract screened, not full proof audit.
sources.paraphrase: Proves convergence under technical conditions for a modified subgradient-based algorithm. It cannot be used as an existing proof for unmodified full BFGS using actual gradients at differentiable accepted iterates.

sources.title: Linear Convergence of Descent Methods for the Unconstrained Minimization of Restricted Strongly Convex Functions
sources.access: Full primary Oldenburg institutional manuscript obtained and relevant assumptions, theorem statements and complete BFGS proof read on2026-09-11; this resolves the earlier abstract-only access limitation.
locators: Assumption3.1 and LS2 equations(3.1)–(3.2), printedp11 / PDFp13
Theorem3.4 and Remark3.5, printedpp13–14; stronger iterate conclusion with uniform matrix assumptions
sources.paraphrase: For convex Lipschitz-gradient objectives restricted strongly convex on the initial level set, Theorem3.7 proves linear full-BFGS value gap and distance to the minimizer set under Armijo–weak-Wolfe and arbitrary SPD initialization. Its proof combines cocoercivity, trace/determinant estimates and AM–GM. No metric-selected limit is identified. Theorem3.4 gives iterate convergence with uniform matrix/inverse bounds.
sources.version_note: Institutional preprint2016-03 cover datedSeptember2016 identifies the final SIAM article. Earliest public date not inferred from filename. Numbered locators refer to this manuscript, not assumed page identity with the journal.

sources.title: The global convergence of partitioned BFGS on problems with convex decompositions and Lipschitzian gradients
sources.first_public_date: 1987 (ANL/MCS-TM-105 predecessor; bibliography evidence, original report not obtained)
sources.access: Primary publisher abstract and publication history read. Full theorem/proof subscription-only, not obtained.
locators: Earlier TM105 title documented in Liu–Nocedal1989 bibliography
sources.paraphrase: Extends Powell to partitioned BFGS and permits Lipschitz gradients in the unpartitioned case. It uses the Byrd–Nocedal potential; potentially singular elements involve damping. Lipschitz gradients concern differentiable objectives, so the earlier semismooth title does not establish gradient-jump nonsmooth convergence.
sources.version_note: TM105 predecessor title: The global convergence of partitioned BFGS on semi-smooth problems with convex decompositions. Precise theorem-level overlap of the smooth subclass remains unresolved.

General all-ray existence of differentiable acceptable points is not asserted.
